label: GPT-6 Astra
output:
Our student-run Winter School on Elliptic Curves and Modular Forms wrapped up on Saturday after three days of lectures, problems and many questions.

Held on 5–7 November 2026 in Seminar Hall 2, Department of Mathematics, Sahyadri Institute of Science, Pune, the school brought together 41 MSc and early PhD students from 9 states. We received 112 applications, with selection based on a statement and one reference.

On behalf of the organising team—Ketaki Joglekar, Faizan Mirza and me—thank you to everyone who made these three days possible.

Thank you to Dr. Nilesh Dharmadhikari (Hyderabad) for the lectures on Mordell–Weil, Dr. Sunanda Iyer (Chennai) for modular forms, and Dr. Tomasz Wierzbicki, joining online from Kraków, for computations in Sage. We are grateful to our faculty mentor, Prof. Anuradha Venkatesan, for her guidance.

The institute’s student initiative grant of Rs 2.4 lakh supported the school, covering hostel stay and travel for 18 outstation students. That support made a real difference to who could attend.

Two moments will stay with me. On day two, a power cut lasted nearly two hours. As laptops ran out of charge, we moved the problem session to the canteen with two rolling whiteboards. It turned out to be our best session of the three days.

An MSc student from Silchar also spotted an error in a worked example in Sunanda ma’am’s notes. She corrected it live and thanked him. It was a lovely reminder that asking questions belongs at the centre of learning mathematics.

A special thank you to Mr. Prakash Salunke, who sorted out hostel rooms at 11 pm after a booking mix-up, and to the office staff. Thank you to our six PhD volunteers for their TA work and problem sessions, and to every participant for joining in so fully.

For MSc students, I think small schools like this can offer something harder to find at big conferences: room to actually ask questions. The PhD-led problem sessions are a format we want to keep.

Slides and problem sheets will be on the department website within two weeks. We hope to run a second edition in late 2027, subject to grant funding. Thank you again, from all three of us.
